# 4-Week Plan: Spreadsheet Automation Course for Office Workers

## Reality check first

You have about 24 hours (4 x 6h) and 300 EUR. That is enough to validate the idea, build a small first version of the course, and get your first paying or beta learners. It is not enough to build a polished 10-hour flagship course and market it. So the goal for these 4 weeks is:

**Ship a Minimum Viable Course (MVP) and get 5-10 real learners (paid or beta) plus feedback.**

Success criteria at the end of week 4:
- A short course (about 60-90 min of video, 5-6 lessons) is live and usable.
- At least 20 people from your target audience have seen the offer.
- At least 3 people paid (or 10 signed up for a discounted/free beta) and you have written feedback from at least 3.
- A clear decision: expand, change the angle, or stop.

## Decisions to make in the first hour (do not skip)

1. **One tool only.** Recommendation: Microsoft Excel with Power Query and simple Office Scripts/macro recording (most office workers have it; no coding needed to get wins). Google Sheets + Apps Script is a possible second course later. Do not cover both.
2. **One narrow promise.** Example: "Stop rebuilding your weekly report by hand: automate cleaning, merging and reporting in Excel in 5 lessons, no coding." Narrow beats broad: a specific pain (monthly/weekly reports, cleaning exported data, merging files) is easier to sell than "learn spreadsheet automation".
3. **One target person.** Example: admin, finance assistant, ops/sales-support staff who already use Excel daily and repeat the same manual tasks. Pick a language (English or your local language) and stick to it.
4. **Price point for the MVP:** 19-39 EUR, or a "founding member" price around 15-25 EUR.

## Budget (300 EUR)

| Item | Cost (EUR) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Course platform | 0-30 | Start on a free/pay-per-sale tier (Gumroad, Podia free trial, Teachable free plan, or Lemon Squeezy). Avoid monthly plans until you have sales. |
| Microphone | 0-50 | Audio matters more than video. A 30-50 EUR USB mic or a decent headset is enough. Skip if you already have one. |
| Screen recording/editing | 0 | OBS Studio, DaVinci Resolve or CapCut are free. |
| Landing page + email | 0-15 | Carrd/Notion/the platform's page; MailerLite or similar free tier. Optional domain ~12 EUR/year. |
| Design | 0 | Canva free. |
| Test ads or promotion | 100 | Hold until week 3-4; only spend after you have a landing page and a clear message. Split across 2 small tests (e.g., LinkedIn or Meta, 5-10 EUR/day for a few days). |
| Excel license (if needed) | 0-20 | Only if you do not already have Microsoft 365. |
| Reserve | 60-100 | Keep unspent. Surprises happen. |

Rule: do not spend on anything (ads, course platform upgrade, fancy equipment) before week 3 checkpoint.

## Weekly time structure (6 hours/week)

Use three 2-hour blocks, ideally fixed in your calendar (e.g., Tue evening, Thu evening, Sat morning). Short regular blocks beat one 6-hour marathon.

---

## Week 1: Validate and scope (6h)

Goal: Know that real people have this pain, and lock a small curriculum.

**To-do:**
- [ ] (0.5h) Write your one-sentence promise, target person, and tool (see decisions above).
- [ ] (2h) Talk to 5-8 office workers (colleagues, friends of friends, LinkedIn messages, local Facebook/Reddit groups like r/excel). Ask: "What spreadsheet task do you repeat every week/month? How long does it take? Have you tried to automate it? What did you try?" Do not pitch yet; collect their words.
- [ ] (1h) Scan competition: look at 5 existing courses (Udemy, Skillshare, YouTube, LinkedIn Learning) on Excel automation. Note price, length, reviews, and what students complain about. Find your gap (e.g., shorter, more practical, real office scenarios, for non-coders).
- [ ] (1h) Draft curriculum: 5-6 lessons, each solving one concrete problem (see sample below). Each lesson = 8-15 min video + one practice file.
- [ ] (0.5h) Write 3 real-world case scenarios you will use as examples (e.g., merge 12 monthly sales files, clean a messy export, build a one-click weekly report).
- [ ] (1h) Create a simple waitlist page + email signup (Carrd/Notion + MailerLite), with the promise and a short description. Free.

**Sample MVP curriculum (adjust to your interviews):**
1. Mindset and setup: what is worth automating (time x frequency), the tools you will use
2. Clean messy data automatically with Power Query (remove blanks, fix dates, split columns)
3. Combine many files/sheets into one table in one click
4. Build a report that refreshes itself (pivot tables + refresh)
5. Record and tweak a simple macro/Office Script for repetitive formatting
6. Put it together: your own weekly report workflow + checklist for what to automate next

**Checkpoint end of week 1 (go / adjust):**
- At least 4 of the people you spoke to describe a repeated spreadsheet pain and have time spent per week.
- If nobody cares, revisit the angle (different pain or audience) before building anything. Do not start recording.

---

## Week 2: Build the core lessons (6h)

Goal: Have lessons 1-3 recorded and practice files ready.

**To-do:**
- [ ] (1h) Create practice files and sample datasets (anonymized/fake data). Make them realistic and messy. Create the "finished" versions too.
- [ ] (0.5h) Test recording setup: audio check, screen resolution 1080p, zoom Excel to 125-150% so it is readable on small screens, close notifications.
- [ ] (0.5h) Write bullet outlines (not full scripts) for lessons 1-3. Know the 3 key points per lesson.
- [ ] (3h) Record lessons 1-3. Aim for under 15 min each. One take per section; keep small mistakes if recoverable. Do rough edits only (cut silence, trim starts/ends).
- [ ] (0.5h) Write a one-page cheat sheet / PDF for each lesson (steps + common errors). Can use Canva/Docs.
- [ ] (0.5h) Send your first quick update to waitlist/interviewees: "Building it, here is a preview of lesson 1" (optional but builds early feedback).

**Tip:** Do not polish. A "good enough" video that solves the problem beats a beautiful one that ships late.

**Checkpoint end of week 2:** Lessons 1-3 are recorded and usable. Show lesson 1 to 2-3 people from your interviews and ask: "Did you understand it? What would you have done next?"

---

## Week 3: Finish the course and build the offer (6h)

Goal: Complete lessons 4-6, set up the platform and landing page.

**To-do:**
- [ ] (0.5h) Apply feedback from the lesson 1 test viewers (pacing, unclear steps).
- [ ] (2.5h) Record and rough-edit lessons 4-6.
- [ ] (1h) Set up the course on your platform: upload videos, files, cheat sheets; add short descriptions; test the checkout and access yourself (buy it with a 100% test coupon if possible).
- [ ] (1.5h) Build the sales page: headline with the promise, who it's for / not for, curriculum, a short demo clip or free preview lesson, price, refund policy (14-30 day money-back reduces risk for first buyers), your short bio and why you are credible. Use the language your interviewees used.
- [ ] (0.5h) Prepare launch material: 1 free lead magnet (e.g., "5 Excel tasks you can automate this week" checklist) + 3 posts or messages (LinkedIn/Reddit/communities where allowed) + 1 email to your waitlist.

**Checkpoint end of week 3:** Course is complete enough to be bought and consumed. A friend can go from sales page to lesson 1 without your help.

---

## Week 4: Launch to a small audience and learn (6h)

Goal: First learners, first feedback, decision.

**To-do:**
- [ ] (1h) Send launch email to waitlist and interviewees with a founding-member price/limited time (e.g., 7 days). Personal messages to the 10-20 people who showed the most interest.
- [ ] (1.5h) Post in relevant communities (LinkedIn, r/excel only if rules allow, local groups, former colleagues). Lead with value (a useful tip/screenshot of a time saved), not a link drop. Respond to every comment.
- [ ] (1h) Optional small paid test: 50-100 EUR for 5-7 days, one audience, one ad, pointing to the lead magnet or sales page. Track cost per signup/sale. Stop if no signal after about 50 EUR.
- [ ] (1.5h) Support first learners: reply to questions quickly, watch where they get stuck, fix confusing parts (quick re-records or added notes).
- [ ] (0.5h) Collect feedback: short survey (3-4 questions: what was most useful, where did you get stuck, what is missing, would you recommend it) and ask for a short testimonial.
- [ ] (0.5h) Review numbers and decide (see below).

**Numbers to track in a simple sheet (practice what you teach):** conversations held, waitlist signups, page visitors, sales/beta signups, money spent, lesson completion, feedback quotes.

**Decision at end of week 4:**
- 3+ paying learners or 10+ engaged beta users and positive feedback: continue. Next 4 weeks: add a bonus module, collect testimonials, improve the sales page, build a Google Sheets version or an advanced module.
- Interest but no sales: test price, headline, or audience; ask non-buyers why.
- No interest after real outreach: revisit the pain (week 1 learnings) or pivot the angle. That is a useful result, not a failure; you spent 24h and under 300 EUR.

---

## Time summary

| Week | Focus | Hours |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Validate, scope, waitlist | 6 |
| 2 | Record lessons 1-3 | 6 |
| 3 | Record lessons 4-6, platform, sales page | 6 |
| 4 | Launch, support, feedback, decision | 6 |

## Main risks and how to handle them

- **Scope creep:** The course grows to 20 lessons. Keep 6 lessons; put extra ideas into a "v2" list.
- **Perfectionism in video/audio:** Set a rule: one re-record per lesson max.
- **No audience:** Your launch depends on your network. Start conversations in week 1 so people are warm by week 4. If you have no network, put more hours into communities and consider the paid test.
- **Falling behind (life happens):** If you lose a block, cut optional items (ads, cheat sheets, lead magnet) first. Never cut the week 1 interviews or the week 4 feedback.
- **Software versions differ (Excel versions, Mac vs Windows):** State the required version in the sales page. Power Query is in Excel 2016+ and Microsoft 365; Office Scripts needs a business/work Microsoft 365 plan, so consider using recorded macros if your audience may not have it.
- **Money:** Only spend the 100 EUR ad budget if the sales page converts at least some visitors from your free traffic first.

## Do this today (30 minutes)

1. Block three 2-hour sessions per week in your calendar for the next 4 weeks.
2. Write down your promise, target person, and tool in one sentence.
3. Message 5 people who use Excel at work and ask for a 15-minute chat this week.
